paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua HaDeromi: in the Jerusalem Talmud, the chapter HaRoeh, Deromaya; also Challah, chapter 1. He spoke before Rabbi Yasa in Rabbi Acha’s name: Jerusalem Talmud, the chapter HaMatznia. Before Rabbi Yonah: Jerusalem Talmud, end of Lulav VaAravah. In the Babylonian Talmud, Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, 30b, Rav Safra said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua Deromaya. I am uncertain whether this is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who lived in the south of the Land of Israel, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi decreed a fast for the southerners. There is some indication of this in the Jerusalem Talmud, end of HaRoeh: Rabbi Yehoshua Deromaya said that the earthly court decreed three things and the heavenly court agreed: Yehoshua’s ban, the Megillah, and greeting with the divine name. At the end of Makkot, 23b, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said that Moses’ court did three things and the heavenly court agreed: the Megillah, greeting, and bringing the tithe. Thus Rabbi Yehoshua Deromaya’s words are the very words Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said in Makkot. But there in the Jerusalem Talmud Rabbi Avun says in Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s name: ‘Also the tithes.’ Thus it appears that the Rabbi Yehoshua Deromaya who said the three things was not Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi. If it is Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, one may explain by the law in Bava Batra 25b: Rabbi Yitzchak said that one who wishes to become wise should turn south; to become rich, north. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: ‘One should always turn south, for by becoming wise one becomes rich, as it says, “Length of days is in her right hand; in her left, wealth and honor.”’ Therefore Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi chose to live in the south of the Land of Israel.
